lines.japanese: 「おう、ドラ！　えらっしゃい！」
lines.english: “Hey, Dora! Welcome!”

lines.japanese: 「たまにはなにか食べてっても、罰は当たりゃあしゃあせんよ？　腹減ってんなら、一つどうだい」
lines.english: “Wouldn't kill you to eat something here once in a while, you know. Hungry? How about one?”

lines.japanese: どの俺が返事をしますか？
lines.english: Which of us will answer?

lines.japanese: 「おう。じゃあここに署名一丁頼むわ」
lines.english: “Hey. Then give me one signature right here.”

lines.japanese: 「あいよっ！　署名一丁お待ち！」
lines.english: “You got it! One signature, coming right up!”

lines.japanese: 「おお。さすがパルさん、仕事が早いわ」
lines.english: “Wow. You're quick, Paru.”

lines.japanese: 「当たり前だってんだ。こちとら江戸っ子だよ？　口より先に手が出らぁ」
lines.english: “Course I am! I'm Edo born and bred. My hands move before my mouth does.”

lines.japanese: 「助かったわ。んじゃ」
lines.english: “Thanks. Later.”

lines.japanese: 「おうっ！　毎度あり！」
lines.english: “Yeah! Thanks for your business!”

lines.japanese: 「小僧！　クレープ頼んでけってんだよ、コンチクショー！」
lines.english: “Buy a damn crêpe before you go, you little punk!”

lines.japanese: 「はいっ！　そんじゃ、ストロベリーにヨーグルトを加えた甘っ甘のやつで！」
lines.english: “Yes, ma'am! Then I'll have an extra-extra-sweet one with strawberries and yogurt!”

lines.japanese: 「あいよっ！　ストロベリーヨーグルト一丁！」
lines.english: “You got it! One strawberry yogurt!”

lines.japanese: 「ええもう、すんっごく甘いやつね。も、甘っ甘のやつで！」
lines.english: “Yes, and make it really sweet. Like, extra-extra sweet!”

lines.japanese: 「おう、甘っ甘のやつで──」
lines.english: “Right, extra-extra sweet—”

lines.japanese: 「──なんかドラが甘っ甘とか言うと気味悪りぃな」
lines.english: “—It gives me the creeps hearing *you* say ‘extra-extra sweet,’ Dora.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「大体あんた、そんなに声のトーン高かったっけ？　なんか妙じゃないかい？」
lines.english: “Was your voice always that high, anyway? Something's fishy here.”

lines.japanese: 「はっ！」
lines.english: “Ah!”

lines.japanese: な、なんてことだ。たかがクレープの注文一つで、怪しまれてしまいました。
lines.english: O-oh, no. One crêpe order was all it took to make her suspicious.

lines.japanese: こ、これはまずいぞ……。
lines.english: Th-this is bad...

lines.japanese: 「しかもなんだい、声から顔つきからヘラッヘラ締まりのないこと、まあ」
lines.english: “And that goofy way you talk, that goofy grin—can’t you pull yourself together?”

lines.japanese: 「滲みでる道化師根性！」
lines.english: “Your inner clown's showing!”

lines.japanese: くっ、ここは隼人君のフリをしてなんとかやりすごさなくては……！
lines.english: Damn it. I need to impersonate Hayato and somehow get through this...!

lines.japanese: 「い、いや、さっきのオーダーはバリクソ冗談なんだぜコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “N-no, that last order was, like, freakin' totally a joke, dumbass.”

lines.japanese: 俺は顎をしゃくりながら、眉間に皺を寄せました。
lines.english: I thrust out my chin and furrowed my brow.

lines.japanese: 「ハードボイルドな俺様が、苺なんて食うわけないんだぜコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “A hard-boiled badass like me doesn't eat strawberries, dumbass.”

lines.japanese: 俺は慌てて先ほどの注文にキャンセルをかけました。
lines.english: I hastily canceled my previous order.

lines.japanese: えーと、隼人君が好きそうなクレープってなんだ？　ハードボイルドっていうと苦味とか？
lines.english: Um, what kind of crêpe would Hayato like? Hard-boiled means bitter, right?

lines.japanese: 「本当に食べたいのは、ゴーヤにコーヒーにサンマのはらわたクレープなんだぜコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “What I really want is a bitter-melon, coffee, and saury-guts crêpe, dumbass.”

lines.japanese: あるわけないですけどね。ええまあ、苦いのが好きっていうアピールをね。
lines.english: Not that such a thing could possibly exist. I was just trying to demonstrate my love of bitter foods.

lines.japanese: （数十秒後）
lines.english: (Several dozen seconds later.)

lines.japanese: 「あいよっ！　ゴーヤコーヒーはらわたクレープお待ち！」
lines.english: “You got it! One bitter-melon, coffee, and fish-guts crêpe!”

lines.japanese: 「なんて！？」
lines.english: “You've got what?!”
“Five hundred yen.”

lines.japanese: 「くっ、バリクソ苦そうだぜコノヤロウ……はい、５００円」
lines.english: “Damn, that sounds freakin' totally bitter, dumbass... Here. Five hundred yen.”

lines.japanese: 自分の内側から「俺、バリクソとか言わねえよ」という声が聞こえた気もしましたが、たぶん気のせいなので無視しました。
lines.english: I thought I heard a voice from somewhere inside me saying, “I don't say ‘freakin' totally,’” but it was probably my imagination, so I ignored it.

lines.japanese: あ、やっぱただのコーヒークレープか……ああ、びっくりした。いただきまーす。
lines.english: Oh, it's just a coffee crêpe after all... Whew, that scared me. Digging in!

lines.japanese: 「で、ドラ。どうなんだい。最近あたしンとこから仕事持ってってないけど、ちゃんと働いてンのか？」
lines.english: “So, Dora. What's the story? You haven't taken a job from me lately. You working properly?”

lines.japanese: ああ、そういえば隼人君、便利屋の仕事なんてやってたんだっけ。で、こちらの春恵姉さんが仲介になってくれてると。
lines.english: Oh, right. Hayato did odd jobs, didn't he? And Harue here found the work for him.

lines.japanese: そうだ、これを利用しない手はない。俺は春恵姉さんに署名用紙を見せました。
lines.english: That's right—why not make use of that? I showed Harue the petition.

lines.japanese: 「ソレなんですけどね。実はいま、知り合いの名前を集めるっていう、特殊な仕事をしてまして」
lines.english: “About that. See, I've got this unusual job right now where I'm collecting the names of people I know.”

lines.japanese: 「ここに名前だけでいいから、一筆いただけませんかね。や、ご迷惑かかるようなことにはなりません」
lines.english: “Could you just put your name down here? It won't cause you any trouble, I promise.”

lines.japanese: きっと人情家の姉さんのことです。署名くらい、すぐにしてくれるでしょう。
lines.english: Harue was warmhearted. Surely she’d sign without any fuss.

lines.japanese: と、思ったのも一瞬。何故か目の前の姉さんは、むっつり口を結んでいました。
lines.english: Or so I thought for one brief moment. For some reason, the woman before me had clamped her mouth shut in a scowl.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あれ？　どうしたんですか、春恵姉さん……」
lines.english: “U-um? What's wrong, Harue...?”

lines.japanese: 「どうしたのじゃねえだろォ、ええ？　呆れたモンだよ」
lines.english: “Don't you ‘what's wrong’ me, got it? You've got some damn nerve.”

lines.japanese: 「なるほどねえ。どーもここンとこ顔見せないと思ったら、他ンとっから仕事もらってたってわけかい」
lines.english: “I see. Was wondering why you hadn't shown your face lately. So you've been taking jobs from somebody else.”

lines.japanese: 「げっ！」
lines.english: “Gah!”

lines.japanese: 隼人君が、どんな契約で春恵姉さんから仕事を請け負っていたかは知りません。ですが、どうやら彼女の不興を買ってしまったことは間違いないようです。
lines.english: I had no idea what sort of arrangement Hayato had with Harue, but I had unquestionably made her angry.

lines.japanese: 「ちっ、違うんですよ？　そういうのじゃなくてですね……」
lines.english: “Th-that's not it! You've got the wrong idea...”

lines.japanese: 「あたしゃねえ、べつにおまえさんが誰から仕事を取ろうが、そんなもんは知ったこっちゃないよ？　だけどさ、それであたしンとこに顔出さなくなるってえのが気に入らねぇや」
lines.english: “Listen. I don’t give a damn who you take work from, understand? What pisses me off is that you stopped showing your face around here because of it.”

lines.japanese: 「ハッ！　別口の仲介が出来た途端、あたしゃハイさようならかい。もう用済みってことかい。ったく、義理も人情もあったもんじゃないねえ」
lines.english: “Hah! The second you find yourself a new middleman, it's so long, Harue. Don't need me anymore, is that it? Not a scrap of loyalty or decency in you.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、世知辛え世の中だ。エエ？　どーなんだいドラ」
lines.english: “Hard times we live in. Well? What do you have to say for yourself, Dora?”

lines.japanese: 「すっ、すみません！　今のはちょっとした言葉の間違いでして、あの、これは仕事でも何でもなく、単なる妹のためのボランティア的な活動で……」
lines.english: “I-I'm sorry! That was just a poor choice of words. Um, this isn't a job at all. It's more like volunteer work for my little sister...”

lines.japanese: 「だったら最初ッからそう言えってんだよコノヤロー！」
lines.english: “Then say that from the start, you dumbass!”

lines.japanese: 「ひいっ！　ごめんなさあーい！」
lines.english: “Eek! I'm sorrrry!”

lines.japanese: 強い女性は苦手です。俺はひたすら謝り倒す羽目になりました。
lines.english: Strong women frighten me. I was reduced to apologizing over and over.

lines.japanese: 「ふむん、屋台か。君主として、下々の生活を知っておくのも悪くないか」
lines.english: “Hmm. A street stall. As a sovereign, it can do no harm to acquaint myself with the lives of the lower orders.”

lines.japanese: 「御免。店主、ヒドラの丸焼きを所望する。タレはいらん、塩でよい」
lines.english: “Pardon me, shopkeeper. I desire a hydra roasted whole. No sauce; salt will suffice.”

lines.japanese: 「ハ？　なんだいそりゃあ」
lines.english: “Huh? What the hell's that?”

lines.japanese: 「るふう、この規模の店では、ヒドラほどの高級食材など用意できぬか。あいや失敬、これは無茶を言った」
lines.english: “Hrrfoo. A shop of this scale cannot procure an ingredient so luxurious as hydra, I see. My apologies. I made an unreasonable demand.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ？　なんだ小僧、あたしの店が小さいって？」
lines.english: “What was that, punk? You calling my shop small?”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、気を悪くするでない。失言は詫びよう、許せ平民」
lines.english: “No, no. Take no offense. I apologize for the careless remark. Forgive me, commoner.”

lines.japanese: 私は自尊心を傷つけてしまった店主に対して、尻を向けてぱんぱんと叩いた（言うまでもなく、ブリュックモント地方において最も敬意を示す謝罪方です）。
lines.english: I turned my rear toward the wounded shopkeeper and slapped it several times. (Needless to say, this is the most respectful form of apology in the Brückmont region.)

lines.japanese: 「そもそもからして、菓子職人に肉を出せという発想に無理があったな」
lines.english: “To begin with, it was unreasonable of me to ask a pastry chef to serve meat.”

lines.japanese: 「菓子職人～？　ハハッ、よしとくれよ、照れるねどーも。そんな大層な呼ばれ方、くすぐってえや」
lines.english: “A pastry chef? Ha! Aw, knock it off, you're embarrassing me. A fancy title like that tickles.”

lines.japanese: 「まあなんだ。そんなおべんちゃら使わなくても、ちったあサービスしてやるからさ。ほら、何がいいんだい」
lines.english: “Anyway, you don't have to butter me up. I'll give you a little extra. Go on, what'll it be?”

lines.japanese: 「ではハウワウパの実を載せたパイを頼もう」
lines.english: “Then I shall have a pie topped with Hauwaupa fruit.”

lines.japanese: 「パウ……なんだって？」
lines.english: “Pow... what now?”

lines.japanese: 「ふぬん、まだ世間では知られておらなんだか。あれはイール山地の高所でしか見つかっておらぬゆえ、庶民が知らぬのも無理はないが」
lines.english: “Hrnn. Is it not yet known to the world? It grows only in the high reaches of the Eel Mountains, so one can hardly fault a commoner for ignorance.”

lines.japanese: 「あの実は滋養と美容によいとされ、三十倍甘くしたキャベツを果実にしたような味なのだ。ううむ、話しているうちに、すぐにでも食べたくなってしもうた」
lines.english: “The fruit is said to promote health and beauty, and tastes rather like cabbage made thirty times sweeter and transformed into fruit. Hmm. Merely speaking of it has made me long to eat it this very instant.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん、よく分かんないけど、うちの店にゃ置いてないねえ。果物屋でも行ってきたらどうだい」
lines.english: “Right. No idea what you're talking about, but I don't stock it. Why don't you try a fruit store?”

lines.japanese: 「うぉんむ、うぉんむ。いずれまた来たりなば、今宵よりはましな食材を用意しておくのだな。もははは」
lines.english: “Wom, wom. Should I visit again, see that you have ingredients superior to tonight's prepared. Mohahaha!”

lines.japanese: 「はいはい。またおいでよ」
lines.english: “Sure, sure. Come again.”

lines.japanese: 「あーったく、金がないなら素直に言ゃーいいのに、つまんねえ意地張っちまってまァ……」
lines.english: “Honestly. If he didn't have any money, he could've just said so instead of putting on that stupid act...”

lines.japanese: そして私は、霊峰たるイールの山々へ向けて旅立った。
lines.english: And so I set forth for the sacred peaks of Eel.

lines.japanese: たわわな果実を両手いっぱいに持ちかえるため。あわよくば野生のヒドラをハントするため。
lines.english: To return with both arms laden with plump fruit. And, with luck, to hunt a wild hydra.

lines.japanese: 他に何か重大な使命があったやもしれぬが、よく覚えていない。旅のさなかに思いだすであろう。
lines.english: There may have been some other grave mission to attend to, but I cannot quite recall it. No doubt it will come back to me on the road.
